title: The fattiest fish and what kind of fat they contain

seo.title: The fattiest fish and what types of fat they contain
seo.meta_description: Mackerel, salmon, herring and sardines contain much more fat than cod or hake. Much of that fat is unsaturated, including marine omega-3 EPA and DHA.
seo.search_intent: Compare fish by total fat and understand saturated, unsaturated and EPA+DHA content.

excerpt: Mackerel, salmon, herring and sardines are among the common higher-fat fish. Representative cooked or canned references often provide roughly 10–18 g fat per 100 g, compared with around 1–2 g in many lean white fish. A substantial share is unsaturated fat, including EPA and DHA.
content_html:
Calling a fish “fatty” does not mean its fat is mostly saturated. Oily fish contain more total fat, while a substantial share is mono- and polyunsaturated, including EPA and DHA.

A representative total-fat ranking

Fish and formApprox. fat/100 gContext
Atlantic mackerel, cooked~18 gVery fatty
Atlantic farmed salmon, cooked~12 gFatty
Herring, cooked~11–12 gFatty
Canned sardines, drained~10–12 gFatty
Trout, cooked~6–8 gIntermediate
Cod or hake~1–2 gLean

Species, season, diet and cooking method can move those numbers, so the table is best read as a scale rather than an immutable league table.

Total fat is not the same as omega-3

NIH lists, per 3-ounce cooked serving, about 1.83 g EPA+DHA for farmed Atlantic salmon, ~1.71 g for Atlantic herring, ~1.19 g for sardines in tomato sauce and ~1.02 g for Atlantic mackerel.

A fish can therefore rank higher in total fat but not in EPA+DHA.

What type of fat is present?

In oily fish, unsaturated fats commonly outweigh saturated fat. Both monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fats are present; EPA and DHA are two long-chain omega-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids.

Does more fat mean more calories?

Usually, yes. Fat provides about 9 calories per gram. A fish with 12 g fat per 100 g receives roughly 100 more calories from fat alone than a fish with 1 g. But calories do not capture protein, vitamin D, B12, selenium or omega-3 value.

Bottom line

Mackerel, salmon, herring and sardines are oily fish because they contain far more total fat than lean fish such as cod or hake, and much of that fat is unsaturated. For omega-3 specifically, compare EPA+DHA rather than total fat alone.

faq.question: Which fish is highest in fat?
faq.answer: It varies by species and form, but cooked Atlantic mackerel can be around 18 g fat per 100 g and exceed many salmon and sardine references.

faq.question: Is fish fat mostly saturated?
faq.answer: No. Oily fish contain substantial monounsaturated and polyunsaturated fat, including EPA and DHA.

faq.question: Does the fattiest fish always have the most omega-3?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Total fat and EPA+DHA are related but do not rank every species in the same order.
